narrative.overview:
True Tunes is a gallery after closing time: dark, quiet walls with album art and artist portraits hung like prints, each with its own caption. The walls are a deep, desaturated navy. Content sits on soft tonal panels a few percent lighter than the ground, never framed or outlined. Colour comes from the work on the walls. The current artwork is blurred into an ambient layer behind the whole app, and the dominant colour of a hero image washes into the card that holds it. The shell (nav pill, player bar, queue sidebar) is frosted glass floating over that layer, so the room takes on the colour of what's playing.

The benchmark is the Apple Music macOS app played straight: no themed or novelty worlds, and the office character lives in people and attribution (who queued what, how often the room has queued it), not in decoration. Type is one family, Manrope, set in sentence case with tight negative tracking on large sizes. Pages size everything in `em` from one fluid base, so the whole page scales from a 1280px laptop to a 3440px ultrawide without breakpoints jumping. Density is relaxed: generous rows, large artwork, nothing cramped.

Every surface now speaks this language: Home, Artist, Album, Playlist, Search, Discover, Leaderboard, Profile, Queuedle, Lyrics, Container, the mini player, skinny mode and the dialogs. The shared primitives live in `components/common/` (see its README) and are the way in: build new surfaces from them rather than from one page's local styles.
keyCharacteristics: One navy tint. Every tonal surface, fill and hairline is `--tint` at a low alpha.
Borderless tonal cards on a tinted ground; artwork is the only thing that casts a shadow inside the content area.
Full-bleed image cards with a bottom scrim and a white caption, like a print and its label.
Accent colour is sampled from the artwork at runtime, never fixed.
Frosted shell materials over a blurred ambient copy of the current art, with solid fallbacks under reduced transparency.
Fluid `em` scaling from one base size; Manrope throughout.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: Every tonal surface, fill, separator and border is `rgba(var(--tint), α)`. To retune the room, change `--tint`; never introduce a second hue for chrome.

rules.name: The Artwork Carries Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour enters only from artwork: the ambient backdrop, the `--wash` radial on featured cards and heroes, the person-header gradient, the player-bar tint. Chrome stays navy and white. Danger and Queuedle's mint are status, not decoration, and are always tonal.

rules.name: The Quiet Wall Rule
rules.body: Tint stays subtle and desaturated. Surfaces sit 6–9% tint over the ground. A wash peaks at 0.3 alpha, with stacked layers counted together (the artist hero's 0.24 radial plus its 0.08 fall-off), and fades to transparent by about 65%. No purple, no neon, no glow.

rules.name: The No Violet Rule
rules.body: Generated colours (avatars, playlist art) never land on 250–330°. Fold the hue past that band rather than clamping to its edge.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Titles, captions, buttons and chips are sentence case. Hierarchy comes from size, weight 600 and negative tracking, not from capitals or a second face. Server strings in title case (tier names) are sentence-cased in CSS.

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: No content text renders below 13px at any window width. 0.93em is the smallest plain `em` step that holds 13px at the 14px base; anything smaller is written `max(13px, Xem)`. Tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) are used for ranks, play counts, facts and times.

rules.name: The Shadows Belong to Prints Rule
rules.body: Inside the content area only artwork casts a shadow. Cards, rows and chips are flat tonal fills.

rules.name: The Frosted Shell Rule
rules.body: Nav, player, queue sidebar, context menu and toasts use the material tokens (`--material-bg` + `--material-filter: blur(30px) saturate(1.8)`). Under `prefers-reduced-transparency` they fall back to solid Raised Navy and the ambient layer is hidden. Don't hand-roll a second glass recipe. The mini player is the one opaque shell, because its window is transparent and frost has nothing to sample: Lit Wall over navy with the wash, and an inset edge only.

rules.name: The No-Outline Rule
rules.body: Content cards, rows, chips, tiles and fields have no border. Separation comes from a tonal step (Wall on navy), not from a line. The only 1px strokes are the frosted shell's separator edge, the artwork's inner keyline, and the shelf search box.

rules.name: The Shared Queue Rule
rules.body: Nothing can replace the shared queue. Every control adds to it; no button, menu item or one-click + sends a replace.

rules.name: The Stations Open Rule
rules.body: Stations open, never add. A station opens as its track list, where songs are added one at a time; it never carries a +.

rules.name: The Not By Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Status colour is always paired with a mark or a word: right and wrong carry a tick or cross, and played days a tick.

dos: **Do** derive every chrome colour from `--tint` at low alpha (Wall 0.06, Lit Wall 0.085, Tint Fill 0.09, Tint Chip 0.16).
**Do** let artwork bring the colour: pass the dominant colour in as `--wash`, cap it at 0.3 and fade it to transparent by about 65%.
**Do** size new surfaces in `em` from the fluid page base and respond with `@container` queries.
**Do** caption imagery with white text over a scrim, never on bare artwork.
**Do** reveal secondary actions (add buttons) on hover or `:focus-within`, and let every interactive element take the global focus ring.
**Do** use the material tokens for anything floating over content, and keep the reduced-transparency fallback.
**Do** use the shared Dialog for every modal, with the primary or destructive action last.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: stop skeleton pulses and image, hero or lyric transitions.
donts: **Don't** use purple, neon or glow, and keep generated hues off 250–330°.
**Don't** set text below 13px or build cramped, dense rows. No sub-13px metadata.
**Don't** outline cards, rows, tiles or fields. Separate with a tonal step.
**Don't** put shadows on content cards. Only artwork and floating surfaces cast them.
**Don't** introduce a fixed brand accent or a second chrome hue. Queuedle's mint stays in Queuedle.
**Don't** use uppercase tracked eyebrows above titles. Hierarchy comes from size and weight.
**Don't** use raster badges with text baked in. A tier is a tonal chip.
**Don't** put a + on a station, or build any control that replaces the shared queue.
